description: Literature chunk fixtures for retrieval evaluation. External chunks (LIT-*) are passages from real, peer-reviewed publications (ACS Catalysis, RSC Advances, Catalysis Science & Technology, Nature Communications, Langmuir). Internal chunks (INT-001 through INT-003) are characterisation-report excerpts whose numerical data are drawn from the same peer-reviewed sources; INT-004 is a synthetic stability-protocol record. Access notes flag values that could not be independently verified from open-access text.

chunks.topic: Pd/CeO2 CO oxidation — activity of atomically dispersed PdOx
chunks.title: Atomically Dispersed Pd–O Species on CeO2(111) as Highly Active Sites for Low-Temperature CO Oxidation
chunks.authors: G. Spezzati, Y. Su, J. P. Hofmann, A. D. Benavidez, A. T. DeLaRiva, J. McCabe, A. K. Datye, E. J. M. Hensen
chunks.text: A 1 wt% Pd/CeO2(111) catalyst, prepared with Pd atomically dispersed as isolated PdOx species anchored on the ceria (111) surface, achieves full CO conversion at temperatures as low as 125 °C. IR spectroscopy of adsorbed CO shows the catalyst is already active at 50 °C. DFT calculations find the elementary step forming CO2 from adsorbed CO and a neighboring lattice oxygen has ΔEact = 29 kJ/mol, while formation of CO2 from the PdO2–CO intermediate has ΔEact = 38 kJ/mol. Metallic Pd is inactive at these temperatures because of CO poisoning; the activity is tied specifically to atomically dispersed PdO/PdO2 sites.
chunks.access_note: Extracted from open-access author manuscript; no numeric TOF or T50 reported in accessible text.

chunks.topic: Pd/CeO2 CO oxidation — sintering/redispersion under hydrothermal aging
chunks.title: Re-dispersion of Pd-based bimetallic catalysts by hydrothermal treatment for CO oxidation
chunks.authors: M. S. Choi, H. Jeong, H. Lee
chunks.text: As-synthesized Pd/CeO2 and Pd-M/CeO2 (M = Fe, Ni, Co) contain Pd nanoparticles 1.7–2.4 nm in size with dispersions of 45.6% (Pd/CeO2) to 64.9% (PdCo/CeO2). Hydrothermal treatment re-disperses rather than sinters the Pd: particle size shrinks to 1.3–1.5 nm and dispersion rises to 75.1% (Pd/CeO2), 86.7% (PdFe/CeO2), 87.4% (PdNi/CeO2), and 88.0% (PdCo/CeO2). PdFe/CeO2-HT shows the lowest CO2 desorption temperature in the series, 87 °C.
chunks.access_note: Data from open-access RSC full text.

chunks.topic: Ni/La2O3 dry reforming — alkali/alkaline-earth promoter effects on conversion
chunks.title: Solution combustion synthesis of Ni/La2O3 for dry reforming of methane: tuning the basicity via alkali and alkaline earth metal oxide promoters
chunks.authors: Y. H. Ahmad, A. T. Mohamed, A. Kumar, S. Y. Al-Qaradawi
chunks.text: ~6.6–7.1 wt% Ni/La2O3 catalysts promoted with Li, Na, K, Cs, or Mg were tested for DRM at 700 °C. Peak CO2 conversion: Mg-Ni-La2O3 (90.8%) > Na-Ni-La2O3 (86.9%) > K-Ni-La2O3 (83.7%) > Cs-Ni-La2O3 (83.0%) > Li-Ni-La2O3 (80.6%) > unpromoted Ni-La2O3 (74.4%). Corresponding peak CH4 conversions: 83.2%, 76.3%, 73.7%, 72.5%, 64.3%, 56.0%. Mg-Ni-La2O3 (surface area 54.2 m2/g, pore volume 0.36 cm3/g) sustained 83.2% CH4 conversion and 90.8% CO2 conversion at 700 °C over 100 h with no detectable carbon deposition.
chunks.access_note: Extracted from open-access RSC Advances full text/SI. All conversion percentages, surface area, and pore volume values are quoted as reported.

chunks.topic: Ni/La2O3 dry reforming — coking resistance and stability decay
chunks.title: Solution combustion synthesis of Ni/La2O3 for dry reforming of methane: tuning the basicity via alkali and alkaline earth metal oxide promoters
chunks.authors: Y. H. Ahmad, A. T. Mohamed, A. Kumar, S. Y. Al-Qaradawi
chunks.text: Over a 100 h stability run, Li-Ni-La2O3 showed 5.0% and 5.7% decay in CO2 and CH4 conversion respectively, while unpromoted Ni-La2O3 exhibited 7.3% and 21.3% decay — nearly four times more methane-conversion loss without a basic promoter. Improved coking resistance in promoted samples is attributed to enhanced surface basicity favoring CO2 chemisorption/dissociation at Ni sites and gasification of carbon deposits via the reverse Boudouard pathway.

chunks.topic: Rh/Al2O3 dry reforming — single-atom loading and reaction conditions
chunks.title: Dry reforming of methane over single-atom Rh/Al2O3 catalysts prepared by exsolution
chunks.authors: M. J. Mekkering, J. Biemolt, K. de Graaf, Y. A. Lin, N. P. van Leest, A. Troglia, R. Bliem, B. de Bruin, G. Rothenberg, N. Yan
chunks.text: Single-atom Rh/Al2O3 catalysts prepared by exsolution were evaluated for DRM at T = 700–900 °C using CH4:CO2:N2 = 1:1:8 at a total flow rate of 100 mL/min. ICP confirmed a loading of 0.005 wt% Rh (found 0.0041 wt%, calculated 0.005 wt%), roughly one isolated Rh atom per 3 nm2 of alumina at the highest loading tested. TOF screening identified 0.005 wt% as the optimal loading at 850 °C.
chunks.access_note: No numeric TOF value (mol CO/mol Rh/s) reported in accessible text, only the qualitative optimum-loading conclusion.

chunks.topic: Rh/Al2O3 dry reforming — coking and pretreatment effects on stability
chunks.title: Dry reforming of methane over single-atom Rh/Al2O3 catalysts prepared by exsolution
chunks.authors: M. J. Mekkering, J. Biemolt, K. de Graaf, Y. A. Lin, N. P. van Leest, A. Troglia, R. Bliem, B. de Bruin, G. Rothenberg, N. Yan
chunks.text: Re-running the DRM experiment improved catalytic activity, with increased yield and stability observed by 850 °C after the first run. Hydrogen pretreatment lowered CO yield by 20%. Methane pretreatment prior to DRM caused severe coking that lowered catalyst performance to that of the plain alumina background reaction — complete blocking of active Rh sites by carbon deposition.

chunks.topic: Cu/(Ce,Zr)O2 water-gas shift — support composition, TOF, and stability
chunks.title: A crucial role for the CeO2–ZrO2 support for the low temperature water gas shift reaction over Cu–CeO2–ZrO2 catalysts
chunks.authors: D. Jeong, H. Na, J. Shim, W. Jang, H. Roh
chunks.text: Co-precipitated Cu catalysts on CeO2, Ce0.8Zr0.2O2, Ce0.6Zr0.4O2, Ce0.4Zr0.6O2, Ce0.2Zr0.8O2, and ZrO2 were compared for low-temperature WGS. Cubic-phase Cu-Ce0.8Zr0.2O2 exhibited the highest turnover frequency and lowest activation energy among catalysts tested, attributed to enhanced oxygen mobility and stronger CuO-support interaction relative to either end-member. This catalyst maintained CO conversion without significant loss during 100 h of reaction.
chunks.access_note: Numeric Ea (kJ/mol) and conversion-vs-temperature table are behind paywall; only the qualitative comparison and the 100 h stability figure are directly quoted.

chunks.topic: Cu/(Ce,Zr)O2 water-gas shift — H2-TPR reducibility across support series
chunks.title: A crucial role for the CeO2–ZrO2 support for the low temperature water gas shift reaction over Cu–CeO2–ZrO2 catalysts (ESI)
chunks.authors: D. Jeong, H. Na, J. Shim, W. Jang, H. Roh
chunks.text: H2-TPR hydrogen consumption (theoretical CuO-only value: 2.50 mmol/g): Cu-CeO2 = 4.22 mmol/g, Cu-Ce0.8Zr0.2O2 = 4.33 mmol/g (highest), Cu-Ce0.6Zr0.4O2 = 3.50 mmol/g, Cu-Ce0.4Zr0.6O2 = 3.20 mmol/g, Cu-Ce0.2Zr0.8O2 = 2.81 mmol/g, Cu-ZrO2 = 2.55 mmol/g (near-stoichiometric). Excess H2 uptake beyond CuO reduction reflects surface ceria reduction and peaks at the same Ce0.8Zr0.2O2 composition that gives the highest WGS TOF.
chunks.access_note: Values quoted directly from openly accessible ESI PDF.

chunks.topic: Ru/TiO2 CO2 hydrogenation — conversion and selectivity, rutile vs. anatase
chunks.title: Interfacial compatibility critically controls Ru/TiO2 metal-support interaction modes in CO2 hydrogenation
chunks.authors: J. Zhou, Z. Gao, G. Xiang, T. Zhai, Z. Liu, W. Zhao, X. Liang, L. Wang
chunks.text: For 2 wt% Ru/rutile-TiO2, air-annealing before H2 reduction raised CO2 conversion at 300 °C from 31.4% to 89.2%, and at 200 °C from 1.9% to 8.8%. This catalyst gave 100% CH4 selectivity between 140–320 °C. The anatase-supported analogue behaved oppositely: air-annealing reduced CO2 conversion at 300 °C from 29.4% to 1.7%, and the air-annealed anatase catalyst gave 100% CO selectivity between 220–320 °C (reverse water-gas shift product instead of methane).
chunks.access_note: Quoted/reconstructed from open-access Nature Communications text.

chunks.topic: Ru/TiO2 CO2 hydrogenation — activation energy and Ru oxidation state
chunks.title: Interfacial compatibility critically controls Ru/TiO2 metal-support interaction modes in CO2 hydrogenation
chunks.authors: J. Zhou, Z. Gao, G. Xiang, T. Zhai, Z. Liu, W. Zhao, X. Liang, L. Wang
chunks.text: Apparent activation energy for CO2 hydrogenation over 2% Ru/rutile-TiO2 (no air pretreatment) was 66.5 kJ/mol, dropping to 40.4 kJ/mol after air-annealing prior to reduction — a ~26 kJ/mol reduction tracking the large conversion gains. XPS Ru 3p Ru+/Ru0 ratio for the air-annealed rutile catalyst rose to 2.2 (more oxidized, better-anchored Ru), while for air-annealed anatase it fell to 0.2 (predominantly metallic, weakly interacting Ru). Higher Ru+/Ru0 (rutile) correlates with the CH4-selective, low-Ea pathway; lower Ru+/Ru0 (anatase) correlates with the CO-selective (RWGS-like) pathway.

chunks.topic: Pd/CeO2 preparation method comparison — XPS surface composition and CO light-off
chunks.title: Internal Characterisation Report — Pd/CeO2 Preparation Series (PdCe)
chunks.text: Three Pd/CeO2 samples (~1 wt% Pd by XRF) were compared across preparation routes. PdCe/IWI (incipient wetness impregnation): Ce3+/Ce = 37%, Pd2+ fraction 81%, PdOx–Ce fraction 19%, Pd/Ce surface ratio 0.060, T50 (CO oxidation) = 159 °C. PdCe/BM250 (ball milling, 250 rpm): Ce3+/Ce = 26%, Pd2+ fraction 24%, PdOx–Ce fraction 76%, Pd/Ce = 0.059, T50 = 120 °C. PdCe/BM850 (ball milling, 850 rpm): Ce3+/Ce = 29%, Pd2+ fraction 55%, PdOx–Ce fraction 45%, Pd/Ce = 0.065, T50 = 185 °C. BET surface area ~50 m2/g and average pore diameter 7.5–8.9 nm across series. H2-TPR: Pd reduction at 127 °C (IWI), 187 °C (BM250), 153 °C (BM850); H2 uptake 565, 1342, 1234 μmol/g respectively. Higher PdOx–Ce fraction in BM250 correlates with lowest T50 and highest H2 uptake, consistent with stronger metal–support interaction.
chunks.authors: M. C. Sánchez-López, M. Á. Centeno, J. A. Odriozola et al.
chunks.access_note: Data from PMC open-access full text (PMC12172315). Sample names abbreviated from paper notation; numbers quoted as reported.

chunks.topic: CuO/CeO2–La2O3 WGS catalyst series — textural properties, Cu dispersion, and stability
chunks.title: Internal Characterisation Report — CuO/CeO2–La2O3 WGS Series
chunks.text: Four WGS catalysts (~10 wt% CuO) were prepared with increasing La2O3 substitution for CeO2. Elemental composition (ED-XRF): CuO/CeO2: Cu 11.5%, Ce 88.5%; CuO/2CeO2-1La2O3: Cu 10.9%, Ce 47.9%, La 41.3%; CuO/1CeO2-1La2O3: Cu 10.2%, Ce 33.0%, La 56.2%; CuO/1CeO2-2La2O3: Cu 9.8%, Ce 24.1%, La 66.1%. BET surface area of calcined catalyst: 90, 86, 57, 23 m2/g respectively. CeO2 crystallite size (XRD): 6.6, 4.8, 3.9, 2.8 nm; CuO crystallite size: 9.9, 13.9, 10.3, 7.0 nm. Cu metallic surface area (N2O-RFC): 61.0, 17.0, 19.5, 16.2 m2/gcat; Cu dispersion: 31.5%, 8.8%, 10.0%, 8.3%. Post-reduction Cu0 crystallite (in situ XRD): 26, 46, 19, 12 nm. After 24 h ideal WGS, Cu0 crystallite in CuO/CeO2 grew to 39 nm (sintering) vs. 12 nm in CuO/1CeO2-1La2O3 (stable). Conversion loss over 24 h: 6% for CuO/CeO2, 3% for CuO/1CeO2-1La2O3.
chunks.authors: E. Rodríguez-Aguado, A. Infantes-Molina, J. A. Cecilia, E. Rodríguez-Castellón
chunks.access_note: Data from PMC open-access full text (PMC11823619). All tabulated values quoted directly from Tables 1–6 of the source.

chunks.topic: Fe-promoted CeO2 support series — BET surface area and particle size vs. Fe loading
chunks.title: Internal Characterisation Report — Fe/CeO2 Support Preparation Series
chunks.text: Six CeO2-based supports were prepared by flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) with Fe loadings of 0–20 wt%. BET surface area and mean particle size (TEM): CeO2: 155 m2/g, 5.3 nm; Fe(1)-CeO2: 171 m2/g, 4.9 nm; Fe(2)-CeO2: 177 m2/g, 4.7 nm; Fe(5)-CeO2: 169 m2/g, 4.9 nm; Fe(10)-CeO2: 166 m2/g, 5.0 nm; Fe(20)-CeO2: 155 m2/g, 5.5 nm. All FSP samples exceeded 150 m2/g. Surface area peaks at 2 wt% Fe (177 m2/g) and returns to baseline at 20 wt%. DFT calculations show oxygen vacancy formation energy drops from 242 kJ/mol (stoichiometric CeO2) to 167 kJ/mol (Fe-doped), a 31% reduction, consistent with enhanced lattice-oxygen mobility and lower CO oxidation barrier (80 → 47 kJ/mol) on Fe-doped surfaces. Pd EXAFS on 1% Pd loaded onto these supports: Pd–Pd coordination number 0.9 (distance 2.81 Å), Pd–O coordination number 4.1 (distance 2.00 Å), indicating sub-nanometre Pd clusters.
chunks.authors: Y. Xie, J. Wu, G. Shi, M. Shen, F. Gao, C. Peng, J. Chen
chunks.access_note: Data from PMC open-access full text (PMC8154324). BET and particle-size values quoted from Table 1; DFT barriers from text.

chunks.title: Internal Stability Protocol — Catalytic Oxidation and WGS Tests
chunks.text: Stability is defined as time on stream before reactant conversion falls below 90% of its initial steady-state value measured at 2 h on stream. CO oxidation tests: fixed-bed quartz reactor (i.d. = 6 mm), 100 mg catalyst diluted 1:3 in SiC, feed 1% CO / 1% O2 / balance He, GHSV = 60,000 h-1, isothermal at target temperature (thermocouple at mid-bed). WGS tests: same reactor geometry, feed 5% CO / 10% H2O / balance N2, GHSV = 30,000 h-1, temperature ramp 150–350 °C at 2 °C/min then isothermal hold. T50 is the temperature of 50% CO conversion measured on the ramp. In situ XRD during WGS uses the same feed at 1 °C/min ramp; Cu0 crystallite size by Scherrer analysis of the Cu(111) reflection.
